title: An unpriced or failed role call costs nothing in the purse, so the cap never binds
body:
## Summary
Budget.charge books a call whose cost is None as free, so a run whose calls come back unpriced (an error after spend, a model missing from PRICES, a CLI that printed no total_cost_usd) is never stopped by its cap.

## Description
cost-metering / price-tables: the default for an unknown cost is 'never zero ... a documented, deliberately high default ... counted'; budget-enforcement: every path that can spend points at a check that sees its target. src/athena/proving/budget.py:105-111 counts the call and adds nothing when cost_usd is None, and can_spend/require (budget.py:93-103) compare spend only. Unpriced sources: NebiusRole returns no cost on an error chunk (src/athena/proving/roles.py, the chunk.kind == 'error' branch) and on its exception backstop; ClaudeRole's timeout and OSError replies carry no cost; tokenfactory.estimate_cost returns None for a model not in PRICES; World.turn's cost_usd is None when no ledger row has a cost (src/athena/proving/world.py TurnRecord.cost_usd), and the Gauntlet charges that (src/athena/proving/gauntlet/run.py:443). Fixed looks like: an unpriced call charges a stated per-engine default (named in an ADR, at or above the dearest known call) for enforcement, is counted as default-priced, and the report keeps the honest absent cost.

## Flow
- a run's Athena-on-Claude turns time out at 300 s (cost None) or the CLI reports no total
- RoleCaller._invoke / gauntlet one(): budget.charge(engine, None) -> calls += 1, spent += 0
- can_spend stays True for every remaining planned call; the --claude-cap never refuses
- fix in build order: UNPRICED_CALL_USD per engine + ADR; charge() books it into an enforcement figure and a default_priced counter; summary() reports both; test 1000 unpriced charges then can_spend False

## Expected impact
The operator whose caps ($1 Nemotron, $10 Claude, ADR 0030) are the only stop on an unattended run; measured by unpriced calls admitted after the cap. Could break: a run with many failed calls stops earlier than today, which is the point, and the default must not be booked into the report's spent_usd.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the purse refuses once unpriced calls could have spent the cap
Before: probe: Budget({nemotron: 1.0}); 1000 x charge(nemotron, None) -> can_spend True, calls 1000, spent 0.0
After: predicted: can_spend False after cap / default calls; report spent_usd unchanged
Method: probe - the Before is measured; the After needs a default price, which is a value an owner names in an ADR, so the round did not pick it
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: src/athena/proving/budget.py:105-111 `if cost_usd is not None and cost_usd > 0: self._spent[engine] += cost_usd`; probe this round: 1000 x Budget.charge('nemotron', None) -> can_spend True, calls 1000, spent 0.0; src/athena/proving/gauntlet/run.py:443 `budget.charge(row.purse, record.cost_usd)`
instrument: tests/proving/test_roles_and_budget.py: N unpriced charges against a 1.00 cap -> can_spend False after cap/default; report spent_usd still the known sum

title: runner.py's hand-kept copies of the CLI's exit meaning and the purse's overshoot both misstate the code
body:
## Summary
proving/server/runner.py repeats two claims from this context by hand, and both are wrong: characters exit 2 'no conversation was held' (the CLI exits 2 when no user turn was judged) and 'a run may overshoot its cap by the one call in flight' (it is one per worker).

## Description
src/athena/proving/__main__.py:16-17 and runner.EXIT_MEANING (src/athena/proving/server/runner.py:131-142) say characters exits 2 when 'no conversation was held', but __main__.py `_characters` returns 2 on `not fidelity['judged']` (src/athena/proving/__main__.py:274), and judged counts user turns the Haiku fidelity judge scored (src/athena/proving/characters/run.py:542-547). Conversations held with every judge call failed (a spent Claude purse, a broken CLI) exit 2 and the hosted page tells the judge nothing was held: copy that names a cause that is not this one. runner.py:15-16 also states the daily cap overshoots by 'the one call in flight', which b92deff corrected in budget.py (one per worker, pinned by a test). Neither copy has a parity test. Fixed looks like: the CLI docstring and EXIT_MEANING say 'no user turn was judged (none held, or no judge answered)', the runner's docstring states one call per worker, and a test pins EXIT_MEANING against the CLI docstring's sentences.

## Flow
- a characters run whose Claude purse is spent before the fidelity judge runs
- _characters: fidelity['judged'] == 0 -> return 2
- runner maps exit 2 -> 'no conversation was held' on the hosted page
- fix in build order: parity test reading __main__'s docstring exit sentences vs EXIT_MEANING (red today only after the docstring is corrected), then both texts

## Expected impact
A hackathon judge reading a hosted run's outcome, and the operator sizing the daily cap; measured by sentences that match the code (0 of 2 today). Could break: nothing executable; the parity test fixes the wording in two places.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the hosted page names the real cause of exit 2 and the real overshoot
Before: 2 of 2 runner sentences misstate the code (traced: __main__.py:274, characters/run.py:547, budget test in b92deff)
After: predicted 0 of 2, pinned by a parity test
Method: simulation - the fix is in proving/server/runner.py, the hosted-server context's file, so the round could not take the After
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/server/runner.py:137-141 `2: "no conversation was held"`; src/athena/proving/__main__.py:274-275 `if not fidelity["judged"]: return 2`; src/athena/proving/characters/run.py:547 `"judged": len(judged)` (user turns judged); src/athena/proving/server/runner.py:15-16 `overshoot its cap by the one call in flight`
instrument: a test in tests/proving/test_server.py that reads __main__'s exit sentences and EXIT_MEANING and fails on a mismatch, plus a run_characters with a control that never answers asserting exit 2's sentence

title: tests/harness's live Nemotron test still runs in a bare uv run pytest when a key is set
body:
## Summary
dd054fb keeps provider tests out of a bare run only under tests/proving; tests/harness/test_tokenfactory.py's live test still reaches Token Factory whenever NEBIUS_API_KEY is in the environment, because CI and AGENTS.md run bare pytest.

## Description
test-harness / isolation-lanes and the suite-partitioning deviation recorded for this context (2026-10-14). tests/proving/conftest.py now skips a provider or eval test unless -m names it, but a non-root conftest's pytest_runtest_setup binds only its own directory. tests/harness/test_tokenfactory.py:616-619 is the same shape (provider marker plus a key skipif), and there is no tests/conftest.py. Fixed looks like: the hook (and the offline fixture, if wanted suite-wide) moves to tests/conftest.py so every provider/eval test in the tree is opt-in by -m.

## Flow
- a developer with NEBIUS_API_KEY in their shell runs `uv run pytest` as AGENTS.md says
- tests/harness/test_tokenfactory.py::test_live_one_turn_against_nemotron runs for both rungs
- two real Token Factory calls are made and billed
- fix in build order: tests/conftest.py with the opt-in hook; the inner-pytest test from tests/proving/test_live.py pointed at it; drop the duplicate from tests/proving/conftest.py

## Expected impact
Whoever runs the suite with a key set; measured by Token Factory lookups from a bare run. Could break: someone who relied on a bare run to exercise the live harness test must now pass -m provider, as README §9 already documents.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a bare pytest reaches no provider whatever keys are set
Before: probe this round: NEBIUS_API_KEY=<fake> uv run pytest tests/harness/test_tokenfactory.py -k live with a resolve-refusing plugin -> 2 lookups of api.tokenfactory.nebius.com
After: predicted 0 lookups, 2 skipped with the -m reason
Method: probe - Before measured; the After needs a file outside this round's paths (tests/conftest.py)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: tests/harness/test_tokenfactory.py:616 `@pytest.mark.provider` + :617 skipif on the key only; no tests/conftest.py (ls); probe log: 2 x `getaddrinfo api.tokenfactory.nebius.com` from a bare run with a fake key
instrument: the inner-pytest test in tests/proving/test_live.py, re-pointed at tests/conftest.py; the resolve-refusing probe over tests/harness

title: A role client that raises leaves no ledger row and takes the run's worker down
body:
## Summary
RoleCaller._invoke calls client.complete with no guard, so any exception a role raises skips the one row README §2 invariant 6 owes every model invocation and escapes the Gauntlet's or Characters' thread pool.

## Description
src/athena/proving/roles.py RoleCaller._invoke: budget.require, then client.complete(system, prompt), then charge; call/call_json write the row only after _invoke returns. ClaudeRole.complete creates its TemporaryDirectory and writes the system file outside its try (an OSError there propagates), and the RoleClient protocol promises nothing about raising. AGENTS.md: 'One row per model invocation, failures included'. The failure path returns before the record its success path writes. Fixed looks like: _invoke catches Exception from complete and returns an engine_error RoleReply naming the type, so the row is written and the worker continues. Risk: tests/proving/conftest.py's generator_answer raises AssertionError as a tripwire ('a generator was asked to judge'); a blanket catch would turn that tripwire into an engine_error row and could let test_gauntlet pass silently, so the fix must keep AssertionError (or a test-only base) propagating, or the fakes move to a recorded flag.

## Flow
- ClaudeRole.complete: tempfile.TemporaryDirectory raises OSError (temp full or denied)
- RoleCaller.call_json -> _invoke raises; no RunLog row, no validity count
- gauntlet one() -> ThreadPoolExecutor.map re-raises -> run_gauntlet ends with no report
- fix in build order: test with a FakeRole whose answer raises RuntimeError -> one engine_error row; then the catch; then re-run test_gauntlet with the tripwire seeded to prove it still fails

## Expected impact
The operator reading a run's ledger after a crash; measured by rows per invocation on a raising client (0 today). Could break: a tripwire fake that relies on raising through the caller.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every invocation leaves a row, failures included
Before: simulation: a FakeRole raising RuntimeError through RoleCaller.call -> raises, 0 rows (traced from roles.py _invoke/_row)
After: predicted 1 row engine_error, run continues; tripwire still fails its test
Method: simulation - the tripwire interaction in another context's test needs its own isolated run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/roles.py RoleCaller._invoke: `reply = client.complete(system, prompt)` with no try; ClaudeRole.complete: `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(...)` and `system_file.write_text(...)` before its try; tests/proving/conftest.py generator_answer: `raise AssertionError("a generator was asked to judge")`
instrument: tests/proving/test_roles_and_budget.py: a raising FakeRole through RoleCaller.call/call_json -> exactly one engine_error row; test_gauntlet re-run with the AssertionError tripwire seeded

title: The bench and the showcase leak a world when a later app's manifest is refused
body:
## Summary
playbooks/bench.py _default_world and adopt/showcase.py _claude_world build a World from the first app, then register the rest; a refused later manifest raises with the world open and its temporary brain on disk.

## Description
923a9ba made World.__init__ close what it opened when its own manifest is refused. The two multi-app factories call world.register(app.manifest()) after construction (src/athena/proving/playbooks/bench.py:141-144, src/athena/adopt/showcase.py:601-604) with no try, and the caller never received the world, so nobody closes it. Fixed looks like: each factory closes the world before re-raising (or World grows a register_all that does).

## Flow
- a playbook whose second app's manifest the route refuses (a bad tool spec)
- _default_world: World(...) ok -> world.register(second) raises WorldError
- the world's brain stays open and athena-world-* stays in the temp dir
- fix in build order: test with a two-app playbook whose second manifest is refused, spy close; then try/except close/raise in both factories

## Expected impact
Whoever runs the bench repeatedly on Windows; measured by worlds left open per refused manifest (1 today). Could break: nothing; the error still reaches the caller.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no open brain or temp root after a refused second manifest
Before: simulation from the code (bench.py:141-144 and showcase.py:601-604 have no cleanup around register)
After: predicted 0 leaked worlds
Method: simulation - both sites are in other contexts (proving-playbooks-bench, adopt)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/playbooks/bench.py:141-144 `world = World(...); for app in rest: world.register(app.manifest())`; src/athena/adopt/showcase.py:601-604 same shape
instrument: a two-app playbook fixture whose second manifest is refused, with build_local spied as in tests/proving/test_world_and_verdict.py

title: extract_json hunts every opener over the whole text, so a 32 kB answer costs 2 s per call
body:
## Summary
extract_json tries raw_decode at every '{' or '[' on a fresh slice of the rest of the text, with no cap on openers tried or on the text scanned, so an unclosed or adversarial answer costs opener-count x length.

## Description
structured-output / extraction-strategies: 'Bound the recovery rungs on both dimensions ... cap the size at which recovery is attempted and the number of openers tried', and the scan is a synchronous loop no timeout can interrupt. src/athena/proving/roles.py extract_json loops `for index, char in enumerate(candidate)` and calls `decoder.raw_decode(candidate[index:])` (a copy per opener). a7a5218 stepped over runs of pure openers; interleaved openers ('[1, ' repeated) still rescan to the end. Fixed looks like: raw_decode(candidate, index) without the slice, a cap on openers tried (a real answer starts in the first few), and over-cap reported as no JSON value.

## Flow
- a degenerate 8192-token answer of '[1, [1, ...' (about 32 kB)
- call_json -> extract_json tries ~8000 openers, each decoding toward the end
- 2 s of CPU per call in a worker thread, doubled by the retry
- fix in build order: timing test over the four adversarial shapes below; raw_decode(candidate, index); opener cap; recheck the widest-value tests

## Expected impact
Run wall time and worker starvation on a bad generator batch; measured in seconds per adversarial answer. Could break: an answer whose JSON starts after more than the cap's openers would be missed (the cap must be measured on recorded answers).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - an adversarial answer is judged in bounded time
Before: probe this round: '[1, ' x 8000 (32 kB) 2.07 s; '{"a": ' x 8000 (48 kB) 1.07 s; x 3000 0.27 s
After: predicted under 0.05 s for each with an opener cap and no slicing
Method: probe - Before measured; the cap value needs recorded model answers to check that no real answer is lost
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/roles.py extract_json: `value, end = decoder.raw_decode(candidate[index:])` inside `for index, char in enumerate(candidate)`; timings this round on the a7a5218 tree: 2.068 s / 1.07 s / 0.274 s
instrument: a timing test over the four adversarial shapes plus the existing widest-value tests, and a replay of recorded ledger excerpts to size the opener cap
